items.headline: CoreWeave bond/CDS distress is the specific trigger behind Friday's Nasdaq-vs-Dow divergence
items.summary: CoreWeave shares fell ~11% Friday after its bonds slipped into distressed territory (some trading near 79 cents on the dollar, Oct-2031 yield above 16%) and its 5-year CDS hit a record ~1,195bp, pricing in a >60% default probability within five years. Because CoreWeave sits at the center of AI-infrastructure debt financing, the scare hit chip/AI names (Nasdaq -2.15%) far harder than the broad, less AI-levered Dow (-0.34%), explaining Friday's unusual index divergence, while VIX jumped 21% to 19.99 on the credit-risk repricing.
items.actionable: This is an AI-financing/credit event, not generic risk-off -- it argues for staying underweight HK/US tech-adjacent exposure while the safe-haven bid it is driving (lower yields, weaker dollar) is directly bullish for the book's gold/silver miner sleeve.

items.headline: China's CXMT DRAM breakthrough keeps extending the memory-chip rout into a second week
items.summary: CXMT's Oct 13 claim of a 4F-square/VSG DRAM architecture rivaling Samsung and SK Hynix continues to weigh on Korean and Taiwanese chipmakers, with the selloff bleeding into HK-listed SMIC via sympathy and compounding Friday's CoreWeave-driven Nasdaq slide. Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix remain the epicenter; the longest chipmaker losing streak since 2008 was still unresolved heading into the weekend.
items.actionable: The CXMT overhang is structural (a genuine competitive threat), not a one-day scare, so any Monday HK-tech bounce should be treated as tradeable relief rather than a signal to add from the cash pile.

items.headline: Brent jumps to $109.69 (+3.56%) as Eurasia Group doubles odds of Hormuz escalation to 65%
items.summary: Eurasia Group raised its probability of a Persian Gulf escalation from 35% to 65% after the container ship GFS Pride was sunk (CENTCOM attributes it to an Iranian projectile; Tehran blames a mine) and Iran-aligned forces reportedly struck targets in Oman; Iran's leadership claimed on state TV that 5-6 vessels are targeted nightly. WTI rose a smaller 1.09% to $99.04, a wider premium than usual over Brent given it is less exposed to Gulf-transit risk.
items.actionable: Rising Hormuz-escalation odds are a second, independent tailwind (alongside the AI-credit scare) for the book's gold/silver exposure via the safe-haven bid, and support the energy-linked names in the SGX offshore/marine sleeve, but raise tail risk for any broad equity add from cash.

items.headline: Gold/silver rally is a Treasury-driven safe-haven bid off the AI-credit scare, not a dovish Fed pivot
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to roughly 5.09% and the dollar weakened Friday as investors rotated out of AI-exposed risk assets and into Treasuries and bullion on CoreWeave-driven debt-financing worries; gold rose 0.40% to $4,186.70 and silver 0.52% to $57.13. GDX (+0.79%) outperforming spot silver reflects miners' operating leverage to the move plus the structural six-year global silver supply deficit underpinning the sector.
items.actionable: Because this leg is credit/yield-driven rather than a Fed dovish pivot, it is fragile -- a clean October 27-28 FOMC hold with hawkish language could unwind part of the yield/dollar tailwind even as it leaves the AI-credit and Hormuz drivers intact.

items.headline: Silver Institute: 2026 marks a sixth straight annual global supply deficit
items.summary: The Silver Institute confirms 2026 will be the sixth consecutive year silver demand exceeds mine and recycling supply, with roughly 762M oz drawn from above-ground reserves since 2021; estimates of the 2026 gap range from ~46M to ~67M oz. Mine supply is structurally rigid because most silver is produced as a byproduct of gold, copper and zinc mining, meaning the deficit cannot close quickly even as prices rise.
items.actionable: The structural deficit is the multi-year fundamental case underpinning the book's silver/miner overweight independent of this week's news flow -- any near-term pullback on a hawkish Fed surprise is a dip to add from cash rather than a thesis change.

items.headline: Fed's Warsh gives no rate signal in Bangkok; CME FedWatch puts ~85-87% odds on an Oct 27-28 hold
items.summary: Speaking at the IMF/World Bank meetings, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to preview the October 27-28 FOMC decision, reiterating the Fed does not do forward guidance, while stressing a commitment to price stability and calling AI the era's most consequential economic shift. CME FedWatch-style pricing shows roughly 85-87% odds of a hold and under 15% odds of a hike, with essentially no cut priced, even after hot September CPI/PPI.
items.actionable: A hold is now the heavily consensus base case for Oct 28 -- the real swing factor for the book's SGX bank/REIT sleeve and gold/silver is less the decision itself than whether Warsh's post-meeting language reads hawkish or dovish given still-hot inflation prints.

items.headline: IEA agrees to release 20M+ barrels from strategic reserves, a bearish offset to the Hormuz oil spike
items.summary: Alongside the Brent rally to near $110, the IEA agreed to release more than 20 million barrels from member strategic reserves in an effort to stabilize supply, while OPEC+ September output rose roughly 900,000 bpd to a 39.07M bpd average. The combination means the Hormuz risk premium is being actively leaned against by both OPEC+ supply growth and coordinated SPR releases.
items.actionable: The SPR release caps how far oil can run purely on Hormuz fear, which matters for the Seatrium/offshore-energy names in the SGX sleeve -- a sustained Brent move materially above $110 would need a real supply disruption, not just a risk premium, to hold.

items.headline: US sanctions Cuban and Iraqi banks over Iran ties; Trump says Iran war will end 'sooner than people think'
items.summary: The US Treasury/State Department sanctioned 16 individuals and 11 entities tied to Iran on Oct 16, including Cuba's Banco Internacional de Comercio for allegedly servicing Iran's Karafarin Bank and an Iraqi bank, part of an escalating financial-pressure campaign running alongside the active Hormuz conflict. Trump separately said the US would not use nuclear weapons or deploy ground troops against Iran but predicted the war would end 'sooner than people think.'
items.actionable: Financial-sanctions escalation without a nuclear/ground-troop threat reads as the US trying to raise economic pressure while avoiding further military widening -- a marginally de-escalatory signal for weekend oil-gap risk, though the active Hormuz tanker campaign remains the dominant near-term driver.

items.headline: MP Materials falls 3.46% to $40.17 despite no company-specific news -- swept up as a high-beta Nasdaq name
items.summary: MP Materials traded as low as $39.88 intraday Friday with no fresh filing, downgrade or rare-earth-policy news to explain the drop; the move looks like sympathy selling as a liquid, high-beta Nasdaq-listed name caught in the broader AI/tech risk-off rather than anything tied to its Mountain Pass/magnetics fundamentals. The stock's underlying business (NdPr sales +127% YoY in Q2, Apple/DoD-backed capex) is unrelated to the CoreWeave/chip credit story driving Friday's tape.
items.actionable: The disconnect between MP's constructive fundamentals and Friday's price action argues against reading this as a rare-earth-thesis problem -- it is a liquidity/beta effect worth fading on continued weakness rather than a reason to trim the rare-earth basket.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control pause nears its Nov 10, 2026 expiry with no decision yet signaled
items.summary: The suspension of five additional rare-earth elements' export licensing (europium, holmium, erbium, thulium, ytterbium, added Oct 9, 2025) is due to lapse Nov 10, 2026 unless Beijing extends it, while seven other elements (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, yttrium) remain under standing license control. No public signal yet on renewal versus lapse as of this weekend, keeping the date as the next hard catalyst for Western magnet/EV supply chains.
items.actionable: With three weeks left to the Nov 10 deadline, the rare-earth basket's near-term setup is a binary policy event -- a quiet extension removes urgency from the Western-supply-chain trade while a lapse/tightening would likely re-rate MP/Lynas sharply higher.

items.headline: Hang Seng/Hang Seng Tech closed Friday's Asia session up before Wall Street's CoreWeave-driven Nasdaq rout
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index rose roughly 0.5% and the Hang Seng Tech Index gained about 1.16% on Friday's Asia session (which closed before Friday's US session), as dip-buyers stepped in after the week's chip-stock selloff and Tencent held steady near HK$417.80. That Asia close does not yet reflect Friday evening's CoreWeave-driven Nasdaq -2.15%/VIX +21% move, which lands as read-through risk for Monday's HK open.
items.actionable: Friday's Asia resilience is stale information by Monday -- expect HK tech to gap against Friday's US AI-credit scare and CXMT overhang at the open, making it a poor entry point for new HK-tech exposure from the cash pile until the open settles.

items.headline: STI closes +0.25% at 5,417.07 as DBS/OCBC/UOB stabilize after the Oct 6-9 yield-driven selloff
items.summary: The Straits Times Index rose 0.25% to 5,417.07 on Friday with positive breadth (127 advancers vs 49 decliners), as DBS, OCBC and UOB traded firmer following their early-October slide tied to the US 10-year yield spike to 5.32%. Friday's STI close predates the evening CoreWeave/Nasdaq rout and Friday's renewed 10-year yield decline to ~5.09%, both relevant for Monday's open.
items.actionable: SGX banks' stabilization is constructive for the book's bank sleeve, but Monday's open will need to digest Friday's US AI-credit scare and Hormuz-driven oil spike, both of which argue for watching the open rather than adding to banks/REITs pre-market.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds near $81,637 into the weekend as crypto trades through Friday's AI-credit risk-off
items.summary: Bitcoin was little-changed Friday-to-Saturday (-0.61% to $81,637) while US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a modest $5.06M net inflow Oct 15 even as Ethereum ETFs saw a further $60.22M outflow, suggesting BTC is drawing relatively more defensive flow than ETH within crypto during the broader risk-off. Saturday Oct 17 also carries options expiry/triple-witching-style positioning unwinds and scheduled token unlocks (ASTER, CRO, DBR), adding mechanical volatility risk independent of the macro news flow.
items.actionable: Crypto's relative calm versus Friday's equity/VIX spike is a useful real-time read that the AI-credit scare has not yet become a systemic deleveraging event -- a break below $80K over the weekend would be the signal to watch before Monday's equity open.
